newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent breaks below $19, WTI market leader.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent breaks below $19, WTI market leader.

text.p: IPE May Brent crude oil lost further ground in the afternoon, breaking below $19 a barrel and brokers expected the contract to push lower before the close.
Trade selling on the NYMEX WTI May/June spread triggered the move down, they said.
"There was some spread selling on the WTI and that pushed us down but we have seen some trade buying taking us off the lows. There is further downside to come though," one commented.
May Brent traded at 1549 GMT down 18 cents at $18.93, just three cents off the day's low. The next support level the contract was expected to test was a recent low of $18.83 a barrel.
April gas oil saw limited volume and eased back with crude to last trade up 25 cents at $165.75 a tonne. The contract traded in a $2 range up from the opening low of $165 a tonne.
"There is really nothing happening on gas oil at all. One decent trade could push it right down, or up of course," another broker said.
Trade for the week so far has been light, dulled by a combination of factors, brokers said.
"It's a whole basket of things - the later opening of the NYMEX, the long Easter holiday stopped momentum and the cash market is quiet as well," one commented.
Overnight weekly stock figures from the American Petroleum Institute gave little momentum to the market.
"There was nothing very surprising there and there is no other news about," another said.
As Europe has moved into summer time NYMEX opens for the week at 1545 British time and closes an hour after the IPE.
"It's (the time difference) killing the market. We really don't expect volume back until next week," he added.
